1.q: וַ⁠יִּקַּ֣ח קֹ֔רַח בֶּן־יִצְהָ֥ר בֶּן־קְהָ֖ת בֶּן־לֵוִ֑י וְ⁠דָתָ֨ן וַ⁠אֲבִירָ֜ם בְּנֵ֧י אֱלִיאָ֛ב וְ⁠א֥וֹן בֶּן־פֶּ֖לֶת בְּנֵ֥י רְאוּבֵֽן
1.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put all the names of the people who **took** before indicating that they **took**. Alternate translation: [And Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, the son of Peleth, the sons of Reuben, took]

1.q: יִצְהָ֥ר & קְהָ֖ת & וְ⁠דָתָ֨ן וַ⁠אֲבִירָ֜ם & אֱלִיאָ֛ב וְ⁠א֥וֹן & פֶּ֖לֶת
1.note: The words **Izhar**, **Kohath**, **Dathan**, **Abiram**, **Eliab**, **On**, and **Peleth** are the names of men.

Here, the word **took** could imply that they: (1) **took** action, or decided to do something. Alternate translation: [took action] (2) **took** men with them. Alternate translation: [took men] (3) **took** confidence or boldness that they should not have had. Alternate translation: [became bold] or [rebelled]

2.note: Here, the author is speaking of opposition as if it were physically rising against Moses. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they opposed]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Moses. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in Moses’ presence]
Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [two hundred and fifty]

The expression **called ones** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, it could be: (1) the other Israelites, who **called** them to participate in important meetings. Alternate translation: [whom the Israelites called to be at important meetings] (2) people at the **meeting**, who selected these men to be leaders. Alternate translation: [whom the people at a meeting had called]

By **called ones of**, the author means they were selected or chosen for a specific purpose. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [chosen ones of]

The author is using **men of name** as a common expression of his culture to mean “respected men” or “men of importance.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [respected men] or [well-known men]

3.note: The Israelites are using **Great to you** as a common expression of their culture to mean “You take too much authority for yourself.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You make much of yourselves] or [You take too much authority]

The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [We say that because]

These two phrases **all of the congregation** and **all of them** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [every single one of the congregation]

Korah and his followers are using the question form to express their disapproval and criticism of Moses and Aaron. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [It is wrong for you to lift yourselves up above the assembly of Yahweh!]

Here, the protesters are speaking as if Moses and Aaron could physically **lift themselves up** above the rest of the people. They mean that Moses and Aaron had claimed authority over the assembly. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [do you take authority for yourselves over the assembly of Yahweh] or [do you claim to be more important than the rest of the assembly of Yahweh]

The author is using the possessive form to describe an **assembly** that serves or worships **Yahweh**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the assembly that worships Yahweh]

4.note: **Fell on his face** was a symbolic action by which Moses showed his grief and humility before Yahweh at the rebellion of Korah and his followers. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. See how you translated the similar words in 14:5. Alternate translation: [lay with his face on the ground to show his grief] or [and bowed with his face to the ground in sorrow]

5.note: The author is using the possessive form to describe a **congregation** that is characterized by following Korah. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and to all the people who had joined him]
Here, the word **saying** introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated **saying** in [1:1](ta:01).

Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Wait for the morning] or [Morning will come]

5.q: וְ⁠יֹדַ֨ע יְהוָ֧ה אֶת־אֲשֶׁר־ל֛⁠וֹ וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠קָּד֖וֹשׁ וְ⁠הִקְרִ֣יב אֵלָ֑י⁠ו וְ⁠אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְחַר־בּ֖⁠וֹ יַקְרִ֥יב אֵלָֽי⁠ו
5.note: These two phrases **Yahweh will make known who is to him and the holy one, and he will present to him** and **whom he chooses he will present to him** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh will make known who is to him and the holy one, and he will present to him. Indeed, whom he chooses he will present to him]

The phrase **to him and the holy one** expresses a single idea. The word **holy one** tells more about who belongs **to him**. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [who is the holy one who is to him]

The implication is that Yahweh will show who truly belongs to him and has his approval. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [who is his] or [whom he has chosen]

5.q: וְ⁠הִקְרִ֣יב אֵלָ֑י⁠ו וְ⁠אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְחַר־בּ֖⁠וֹ יַקְרִ֥יב אֵלָֽי⁠ו
5.note: The implication is that Yahweh will enable certain people to come into his presence and serve him. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and he will enable to come near to himself, and whom he chooses he will enable to come near to himself]

Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and he will present that person to him]

6.note: A **censer** is a kind of container used for burning incense. If your readers would not be familiar with what a censer is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [containers for incense]

Here Moses is using the possessive form to describe a **congregation** that is characterized by following Korah. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. See how you translated the similar form in verse 5. Alternate translation: [and all the people who have joined him]

7.note: Here, **fire** represents burning coals. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [embers]
Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

It might seem that the expression **the man whom Yahweh chooses, he is the holy one** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [the man whom Yahweh chooses is the holy one]

Moses is using the phrase **Great to you** as a common expression of his culture to mean “You take too much authority” or “You make too much of yourselves.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in verse 3. Alternate translation: [You make much of yourselves] or [You take too much authority]

Here, Moses is speaking as if all the people who were descended from Levi were actually **sons of Levi**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [men descended from Levi]

8.note: Here, Moses continues speaking with Korah. The author states that Moses addressed **Korah** specifically, but Moses also addresses all the Levites who are with Korah. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could indicate more explicitly that Moses continues to speak, addressing himself directly to Korah but including other Levites as well. Alternate translation: [And Moses continued to speak with Korah as well as the Levites who were with him. He said]

Moses is speaking of the tribe of Levi as if they were literally the **sons of Levi**. They were actually his descendants. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated this phrase in verse 7. Alternate translation: [men descended from Levi]

9.q: הַ⁠מְעַ֣ט מִ⁠כֶּ֗ם כִּֽי־הִבְדִּיל֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶתְ⁠כֶם֙ מֵ⁠עֲדַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְ⁠הַקְרִ֥יב אֶתְ⁠כֶ֖ם אֵלָ֑י⁠ו לַ⁠עֲבֹ֗ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַת֙ מִשְׁכַּ֣ן יְהוָ֔ה וְ⁠לַ⁠עֲמֹ֛ד לִ⁠פְנֵ֥י הָ⁠עֵדָ֖ה לְ⁠שָׁרְתָֽ⁠ם׃ וַ⁠יַּקְרֵב֙ אֹֽתְ⁠ךָ֔ וְ⁠אֶת־כָּל־אַחֶ֥י⁠ךָ בְנֵי־לֵוִ֖י אִתָּ֑⁠ךְ וּ⁠בִקַּשְׁתֶּ֖ם גַּם־כְּהֻנָּֽה
9.note: The question that begins in 16:9 could end at: (1) the end of verse 9. In this case, verse 10 is its own question. See the ULT. (2) the words **the sons of Levi, with you** in verse 10. Alternate translation: [Is it small from you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel to present you to him to serve the service of the Dwelling of Yahweh and to stand to the face of the congregation to minister to them and has presented you and all your brothers, the sons of Levi, with you? But do you seek the priesthood also?]

9.q: הַ⁠מְעַ֣ט מִ⁠כֶּ֗ם כִּֽי־הִבְדִּיל֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶתְ⁠כֶם֙ מֵ⁠עֲדַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְ⁠הַקְרִ֥יב אֶתְ⁠כֶ֖ם אֵלָ֑י⁠ו לַ⁠עֲבֹ֗ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַת֙ מִשְׁכַּ֣ן יְהוָ֔ה וְ⁠לַ⁠עֲמֹ֛ד לִ⁠פְנֵ֥י הָ⁠עֵדָ֖ה לְ⁠שָׁרְתָֽ⁠ם
9.note: Moses is using the question form to rebuke Korah for not being content with his role. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should not consider it small from you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel to present you to him to serve the service of the Dwelling of Yahweh and to stand to the face of the congregation to minister to them!]

Moses is using **Is it small from you** as a common expression of his culture to mean “Do you consider it insignificant?” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Do you consider it insignificant]

The author is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to serve]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as the Dwelling of Yahweh needs to be served]

Here, Moses is speaking of the Levites serving in front of the congregation as if they were standing **to the face** of the congregation. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and to be ready to serve the congregation]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the congregation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before the congregation]

10.note: The implication is that God enabled the Levites to serve at his sanctuary. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated the similar phrases in verse 5. Alternate translation: [And he has enabled you and all your brothers, the sons of Levi, with you to come near to himself]

The word **you** is singular in most of this verse because Moses is speaking to Korah, but in **you seek** it is plural because Moses is speaking about Korah and his fellow Levites. Use the correct singular and plural forms in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Here, Moses is using the term **brothers** to describe people who are descended from the same ancestor. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and all your relatives]

Here, Moses is speaking as if the people of the tribe of Levi were literally the **sons of Levi**. They were actually his descendants. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated this phrase in verse 7. Alternate translation: [the men descended from Levi]

Moses is using the question form to express disapproval of Korah’s desire for the priesthood. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [but you are seeking the priesthood also!] or [and despite that you are seeking the priesthood also.]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **priesthood**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to serve as priests]

11.note: In this verse, forms of **you** are singular except for the word **you** in **you murmur**, which is plural because it refers to both Korah and his followers. So use the plural form in that place in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Moses is using the possessive form to describe a **congregation** that is characterized by following Korah. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. See how you translated the similar words in verse 5. Alternate translation: [and all the people who have joined you]

Moses is using the question form to emphasize that Aaron is not really the one they are rebelling against. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [and Aaron is not actually the one whom you are murmuring against] or [and since Yahweh appointed Aaron, Aaron is not the one whom you are actually murmuring against]

It might seem that the expression **and Aaron, what is he** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [and what is Aaron that]

12.note: The implication is that Moses sent someone to call Dathan and Abiram. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And Moses sent someone to call]
The words **Dathan** and **Abiram** are the names of men, and **Eliab** is also the name of a man. See how you translated these names in [verse 1](ta:16).

Dathan and Abiram are using **go up** as a common expression of their culture to mean “present ourselves to you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [We will not present ourselves to you]

13.q: הַ⁠מְעַ֗ט כִּ֤י הֶֽעֱלִיתָ֨⁠נוּ֙ מֵ⁠אֶ֨רֶץ זָבַ֤ת חָלָב֙ וּ⁠דְבַ֔שׁ לַ⁠הֲמִיתֵ֖⁠נוּ בַּ⁠מִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּֽי־תִשְׂתָּרֵ֥ר עָלֵ֖י⁠נוּ גַּם־הִשְׂתָּרֵֽר
13.note: Dathan and Abiram are using the question form to express indignation at Moses’ leadership. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should not consider it so small that you have brought us up from a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness that you make yourself rule over us, also making yourself rule!]

The phrase **Is it small that** is a common expression of this culture that means “Do you consider it insignificant that” or “Is it not enough that.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in verse 9. Alternate translation: [Do you consider it so insignificant that]

Here, Dathan and Abiram are speaking of Egypt as if it were a land actually **flowing with milk and honey**. This was a way of saying that it was a very fertile and productive place. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 13:27. Alternate translation: [from a land that is rich and fertile] or [from a land that is very productive]

Dathan and Abiram are repeating forms of the verb **rule** in order to intensify their expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [you make yourself rule over us completely]

14.note: Here, Dathan and Abiram are speaking as if the land were actually **flowing with milk and honey**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in verse 13. Alternate translation: [to a land that is rich and fertile] or [to a land that is very productive]

Dathan and Abiram are using the term **inheritance** by association to mean a lasting possession that would be passed down to future generations. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [a lasting possession of]

Here, **field** and **vineyard** represent agricultural land in general, not specific fields and vineyards. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use expressions that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [of fields and vineyards]

Dathan and Abiram are using the question form to make a strong negative statement. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You cannot gouge out the eyes of these men!]

Here, Dathan and Abiram are speaking of deceiving people as if it were **gouging out** their eyes. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Will you mislead these men] or [Will you trick these men]
See how you translated this clause in 16:12. Alternate translation: [We will not present ourselves to you]

15.note: The author is using **it burned exceedingly** as a common expression of this culture to mean “he became very angry.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and Moses’ anger burned greatly] or [and Moses was enraged]

Here, Moses is speaking of accepting an offering as if Yahweh would **turn to** look at it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Do not receive]

By **grain offering**, Moses means any offering from them at all. He is using a grain offering as an example because it was a small offering. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [any offering from them, even a grain offering]

Here, Moses is speaking of stealing as if it were lifting something up. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have not stolen one donkey from them]

By **one donkey**, Moses means he has not taken anything from the Israelites, not even something as insignificant as a donkey. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [something as insignificant as one donkey]

16.note: Moses is using the possessive form to describe a **congregation** that is characterized by following Korah. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. See how you translated this phrase in verse 11. Alternate translation: [all the people who have joined you]
Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

17.q: וּ⁠קְח֣וּ ׀ אִ֣ישׁ מַחְתָּת֗⁠וֹ וּ⁠נְתַתֶּ֤ם עֲלֵי⁠הֶם֙ קְטֹ֔רֶת וְ⁠הִקְרַבְתֶּ֞ם לִ⁠פְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ אִ֣ישׁ מַחְתָּת֔⁠וֹ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּ⁠מָאתַ֖יִם מַחְתֹּ֑ת
17.note: It might seem that the second occurrence of the expression **a man his censer** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [And take a man his censer, and put incense on them, and present to the face of Yahweh, 250 censers]

Moses is using **take a man his censer** as a common expression of his culture to mean “each man must take his censer.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And all the men must take their censers]

A **censer** is a kind of metal container used for burning incense. If your readers would not be familiar with what a censer is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. See how you translated **censer** in verse 6. Alternate translation: [his container for incense … his container for incense … containers for incense … his container for incense]
Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]
Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [two hundred and fifty]

Moses is using **a man his censer** as a common expression of his culture to mean “each person with his own censer.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all the men with their censers … each with your own censer]

18.note: Moses is using **a man his censer** as a common expression of his culture to mean “each man took his own censer.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar words in verse 17. Alternate translation: [And all the men took their censers]

18.q: וַֽ⁠יַּעַמְד֗וּ פֶּ֛תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד וּ⁠מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְ⁠אַהֲרֹֽן
18.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **Moses and Aaron** with the information about the others who stood at the entrance. Alternate translation: [and they and Moses and Aaron stood at the opening of the tent of meeting]

19.note: Here, the **congregation** could be: (1) the Israelite community. Alternate translation: [all the Israelite congregation] (2) just the men with Korah, referred to as “his congregation” in 16:5. Alternate translation: [all his congregation] or [all his followers]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **glory**, you could express the same idea in another way. See how you translated the similar clause in 14:10. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh showed himself gloriously]

21.note: Yahweh is using **I shall finish them** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will make them die” or “I will cause them to cease to exist.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I shall end their lives] or [and I will make them experience death]

Yahweh is using **according to a moment** as a common expression of the culture to mean “instantly” or “immediately.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [instantly]

22.note: Falling on their faces was a symbolic action by which Moses and Aaron showed their grief and submission to God. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. See how you translated the similar words in chapter 14:5. Alternate translation: [And they lay with their faces on the ground to show their grief] or [And they bowed with their faces to the ground in sorrow]

The author is using the possessive form to describe **God** who gives or rules the **spirits** that belong to or are in **all flesh**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the God who rules the spirits in all flesh] or [the God who gave the spirits to all flesh]

Moses and Aaron are using **the spirits of all flesh** as a common expression of their culture to mean “the life that is in all living things.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the life that is in all living things] or [everything that lives]

22.q: הָ⁠אִ֤ישׁ אֶחָד֙ יֶחֱטָ֔א וְ⁠עַ֥ל כָּל־הָ⁠עֵדָ֖ה תִּקְצֹֽף
22.note: Moses and Aaron are using the question form to protest the unfairness of punishing everyone for one person’s sin. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [when one man sins, surely you will not be angry against all the congregation.]

24.q: דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל־הָ⁠עֵדָ֖ה לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר הֵֽעָלוּ֙ מִ⁠סָּבִ֔יב לְ⁠מִשְׁכַּן־קֹ֖רַח דָּתָ֥ן וַ⁠אֲבִירָֽם
24.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Tell the congregation that they must be taken up from around to the dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.]

The expression **Be taken up** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is the Israelites. Alternate translation: [Take yourselves up]

Here, Yahweh is speaking of moving away from Korah’s dwelling as if people could be **taken up** from that place. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Move away]

By **from around to the dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram**, Yahweh means that the people should move away from all sides of where these men were living. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [from the dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram on every side]

25.note: The author is using **rose** as a common expression of the culture to mean “began to do something.” He is not saying that Moses got up from a seated position. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Moses got ready]
In a context such as this, your language might say “came” instead of **went**. Alternate translation: [and came]

26.note: Moses is using **from upon the tents of** as a common expression of his culture to mean “from near the tents of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from near the tents of]

Moses is using the word translated as **lest** to introduce an outcome that he does not want to happen. Because of this, he first gives the people an instruction to follow so that this will not happen. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that avoiding this outcome is the purpose of the instruction. Alternate translation: [or else you will be swept away]

Here, Moses is speaking as if the punishment of others’ sins were a flood that could **sweep away** those who are nearby. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you be included when God punishes them for their sins] or [you too experience the punishment for their sins]

27.note: The expression **were taken up** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is the Israelites. See how you translated the similar form in verse 24. Alternate translation: [And they took themselves up]

Here, the author is speaking of moving physically away from a place as if the people were being **taken up**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar form in verse 24. Alternate translation: [And they moved away]

The expression **from upon the dwelling of** is a common expression of the culture that means “from the area around” or “from near.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar form in verse 26. Alternate translation: [from near the dwelling of]

The implication is that the people moved away from all sides of where the men were living. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. (See how you translated the similar phrase in verse 24.) Alternate translation: [on every side]

27.q: וְ⁠דָתָ֨ן וַ⁠אֲבִירָ֜ם יָצְא֣וּ נִצָּבִ֗ים פֶּ֚תַח אָֽהֳלֵי⁠הֶ֔ם וּ⁠נְשֵׁי⁠הֶ֥ם וּ⁠בְנֵי⁠הֶ֖ם וְ⁠טַפָּֽ⁠ם
27.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about the wives, sons, and children with the information about **Dathan and Abiram** before saying that they were **standing at the opening of their tents**. Alternate translation: [and Dathan and Abiram and their wives and their sons and their children went out, standing at the opening of their tents]

Here, the author implies that Dathan, Abiram, and their families **went out** of their tents before the Israelites moved away from them. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could make the sequence of events more explicit. Alternate translation: [and meanwhile, Dathan and Abiram had gone out]
The implication is that Dathan and Abiram **went out** of their tents. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [went out of their tents]
In a context such as this, your language might say “came” instead of **went out**. Alternate translation: [came out]

The implication is that **their sons** and **their children** refer to the same group, with the second phrase being more general. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and their sons and the rest of their children]

28.note: The phrase **By this** refers to what Moses is about to say in verses 29–30. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [By what I am about to say]

Here, **heart** represents Moses’ own thoughts, desires, or will. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from my own prompting] or [from my own choice]

29.q: כְּ⁠מ֤וֹת כָּל־הָֽ⁠אָדָם֙ יְמֻת֣וּ⁠ן אֵ֔לֶּה וּ⁠פְקֻדַּת֙ כָּל־הָ֣⁠אָדָ֔ם יִפָּקֵ֖ד עֲלֵי⁠הֶ֑ם
29.note: These two phrases **as the death of every man these die** and **the oversight of every man is counted upon them** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [as the death of every man these die in an ordinary way]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **death**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as every man dies]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [every human … every human]

Moses is referring to death in a polite way by using the phrase **the oversight of every man is counted upon them**. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [and the fate of every man happens to them] or [and they experience death like everyone else does]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **oversight**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and how every man is overseen]

Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [then you will know that Yahweh did not send me]

30.note: Moses is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [creates something] or [makes a creation]

By **a creation**, Moses means something that has never happened before. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a new thing]

Moses is speaking of **the ground** as if it were a living thing that could open its mouth and swallow. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and a hole forms in the ground and engulfs them]

Here, Moses is speaking of death as if it were going to a place called **Sheol** that these people would enter while still alive. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it is as if they arrive at the place of the dead while they are still alive] or [and they die after they are buried instead of before]

31.note: The expression **was split open** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is the ground. Alternate translation: [split open] or [broke apart]
The pronoun **them** refers to Dathan, Abiram, and their families. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [under Dathan, Abiram, and their families]

32.note: The author is speaking of **the earth** as if it were a living thing that could open its mouth and swallow people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar clause in verse 30. Alternate translation: [and a hole formed in the earth and engulfed them]

32.q: וְ⁠אֶת־בָּתֵּי⁠הֶ֑ם וְ⁠אֵ֤ת כָּל־הָ⁠אָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְ⁠קֹ֔רַח וְ⁠אֵ֖ת כָּל־הָ⁠רֲכֽוּשׁ
32.note: Here, **every man** and **all the property** could refer to: (1) people and their property in addition to Dathan, Abiram, and their families. These people agreed with Korah, but they were not among the 250 men who offered incense at the sacred tent. Alternate translation: [and their houses, and in addition every man who was to Korah besides the 250 men and all their property] (2) Dathan, Abiram, and their families. The author is simply giving more information about them. Alternate translation: [and their houses, that is, every man who was to Korah and all their property]

Here, the author is speaking of the people and animals and objects that belonged to these men as if they were **houses** in which they lived. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and their households]

The author is using **who was to Korah** as a common expression of the culture to mean “who had followed Korah” or “who had supported Korah.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and every man who had followed Korah]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [and every person]

33.q: וַ⁠יֵּ֨רְד֜וּ הֵ֣ם וְ⁠כָל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָ⁠הֶ֛ם חַיִּ֖ים שְׁאֹ֑לָ⁠ה
33.note: Here, the author is speaking of death as if it were going to a place called **Sheol** that these people would enter while still alive. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar clause in verse 30. Alternate translation: [and it as if they arrived, they and all that was to them, at the place of the dead while they were still alive] or [and they died, they and all that was to them, after they were buried instead of before]

The author is speaking of **the earth** as if it were a living thing that could cover people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they were covered with earth]

34.note: Here, **all Israel** represents each member of the Israelite community. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And each Israelite]

The implication is that the Israelites fled because they heard the screams of those who were falling into the opening in the ground. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [because of their yells as they fell] or [when they heard them shouting as they fell]

Here, **to their voice** represents the sounds they made when the ground opened and swallowed them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to the sounds they made]

The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [and here is why: they said]

The implication is that the Israelites would die if they did not run away. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [If we do not flee, the earth will swallow us]

The author is speaking of **the earth** as if it were a living thing that could swallow people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar clause in verse 30. Alternate translation: [the earth engulf them]

35.note: The author does not clarify whether the event narrated in this verse happened during or after the events narrated in the previous verses. If possible, do not use a time word or phrase to introduce this verse. Alternate translation: [In addition, fire went out]
In a context such as this, your language might say “came out” instead of **went out**. Alternate translation: [came out]

Here the author is speaking of **fire** as if it were a living thing that could eat. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it burned up]
Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [two hundred and fifty]

37.q: אֱמֹ֨ר אֶל־אֶלְעָזָ֜ר בֶּן־אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֗ן וְ⁠יָרֵ֤ם אֶת־הַ⁠מַּחְתֹּת֙ מִ⁠בֵּ֣ין הַ⁠שְּׂרֵפָ֔ה וְ⁠אֶת־הָ⁠אֵ֖שׁ זְרֵה־הָ֑לְאָה כִּ֖י קָדֵֽשׁוּ
37.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the last phrase **for they are holy** gives the reason for the result that the first phrases describe. Alternate translation: [The censers are holy. Because of that, say to Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, and he shall raise the censers from between the burning, and scatter the fire beyond]

37.q: אֱמֹ֨ר אֶל־אֶלְעָזָ֜ר בֶּן־אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֗ן וְ⁠יָרֵ֤ם אֶת־הַ⁠מַּחְתֹּת֙ מִ⁠בֵּ֣ין הַ⁠שְּׂרֵפָ֔ה וְ⁠אֶת & זְרֵה
37.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as a direct quotation. Alternate translation: [Tell Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, “Raise the censers from between the burning.” And scatter]

A **censer** is a kind of container used to burn incense. If your readers would not be familiar with what a censer is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. See how you translated **censer** in verse 6. Alternate translation: [the containers for incense]

The implication is that the censers were to be taken from among the ashes and remains of the men who had been burned up. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [from the place where the men were burned up]

Here, Yahweh may be commanding Moses: (1) to **scatter the fire** himself. Alternate translation: [and you, scatter the fire] (2) to have Eleazar **scatter the fire**. Alternate translation: [and he shall scatter the fire]
Here, **fire** represents the burning coals. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the embers]

Here, the word **beyond** could refer to: (1) an area far away from the campsite. Alternate translation: [a distance from the camp] (2) a spread out area. In other words, the coals should be scattered in many different places. Alternate translation: [far and wide] or [in many places]

38.q: אֵ֡ת מַחְתּוֹת֩ הַֽ⁠חַטָּאִ֨ים הָ⁠אֵ֜לֶּה בְּ⁠נַפְשֹׁתָ֗⁠ם וְ⁠עָשׂ֨וּ אֹתָ֜⁠ם רִקֻּעֵ֤י פַחִים֙ צִפּ֣וּי לַ⁠מִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כִּֽי־הִקְרִיבֻ֥⁠ם לִ⁠פְנֵֽי־יְהוָ֖ה וַ⁠יִּקְדָּ֑שׁוּ
38.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [These ones sinning against their lives presented the censers to the face of Yahweh, and they are holy. Because of that, they shall make them hammered sheets of thin plates, plating for the altar]

38.q: אֵ֡ת מַחְתּוֹת֩ הַֽ⁠חַטָּאִ֨ים הָ⁠אֵ֜לֶּה בְּ⁠נַפְשֹׁתָ֗⁠ם וְ⁠עָשׂ֨וּ אֹתָ֜⁠ם רִקֻּעֵ֤י פַחִים֙
38.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about what should be done with the censers before the information about how these men sinned. Alternate translation: [And they shall make the censers of these ones sinning against their lives hammered sheets of thin plates]

Yahweh is using **ones sinning against their lives** as a common expression of the culture to mean “ones who caused their own deaths by sinning.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [ones sinning in a way that ends their lives] or [ones sinning with death as the result]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **lives**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in such a way that they cease living]

Here Yahweh is using the pronoun **they** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people shall make]

Here, **hammered sheets of thin plates** are a kind of metalwork where metal is flattened into very thin pieces. If your readers would not be familiar with what hammered sheets of thin plates are, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [thin sheets of metal that they hammered into that shape]

Here, **plating** is a kind of thin metal that is attached to the outside of something, in this case the altar. If your readers would not be familiar with what **plating** is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [close-fitting covering for the altar]

Here, Yahweh does not state explicitly which **altar** he means. He is probably referring to the bronze altar for sacrifices, not the golden incense altar. Alternate translation: [for the altar of sacrifice]
Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

The pronoun **they** refers to the censers that were hammered into plating for the altar. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the censers that are now plating for the altar shall be]

39.note: The expression **ones being burned** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [the ones whom the fire burned]

Here the author is using the pronoun **they** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. See how you translated the similar form in verse 38. Alternate translation: [and people hammered them]
See how you translated this phrase in 16:38. Alternate translation: [close-fitting covering for the altar of sacrifice]

40.q: זִכָּר֞וֹן לִ⁠בְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְ֠מַעַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־יִקְרַ֜ב אִ֣ישׁ זָ֗ר אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹ֣א מִ⁠זֶּ֤רַע אַהֲרֹן֙ ה֔וּא לְ⁠הַקְטִ֥יר קְטֹ֖רֶת לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְ⁠לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֤ה כְ⁠קֹ֨רַח֙ וְ⁠כַ֣⁠עֲדָת֔⁠וֹ כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בְּ⁠יַד־מֹשֶׁ֖ה לֽ⁠וֹ
40.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about how **Yahweh spoke in the hand of Moses** with the information about how Eleazar was instructed before indicating that the plating would serve as a memorial to prevent unauthorized people from offering incense. Alternate translation: [just as Yahweh spoke in the hand of Moses to him. They became a memorial for the sons of Israel, so that a strange man, who is not from the seed of Aaron, shall not come near to cause incense to become smoke to the face of Yahweh, and he shall not be like Korah and like his congregation]

Here, **strange** describes a person as if he were a foreigner when he actually is simply someone who is not authorized to perform the duties of a priest. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase “strange fire” in Numbers 3:4. Alternate translation: [an unauthorized man]

Here, the author is speaking as if Aaron’s descendants were actually his **seed**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the offspring of Aaron]

Here, **to the face of Yahweh** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

The phrase **and he shall not be** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [lest he be] or [and so he shall not be]

The point of this comparison is that just as **Korah and his congregation** were punished for approaching God inappropriately, so would anyone else be who violated this command. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [punished as Korah and his congregation were]

The author is using the possessive form to describe a **congregation** that is characterized by following Korah. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. See how you translated the similar form in verse 5. Alternate translation: [the people who joined him]

The author is using **in the hand of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “under the supervision of” or “through.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 4:37. Alternate translation: [under the supervision of Moses]
The pronoun **him** refers to Eleazar. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to Eleazar]

41.note: The author is using **from the next day** as a common expression of the culture to mean “starting on the next day.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [starting on the next day]

Here the Israelites are stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though they repeat it twice for emphasis. The Israelites are emphasizing that they hold Moses and Aaron personally responsible. If a speaker of your language would use a repeated pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing that meaning here. Alternate translation: [You are the one who killed]

The Israelites are using the possessive form to describe **people** that are characterized by serving or worshiping **Yahweh**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the people who serve Yahweh] or [the people who worship Yahweh]

42.note: The author is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [and look, the cloud] or [and they immediately noticed that the cloud]

By **the cloud covered it**, the author means that the cloud that represented God’s presence descended upon the tent of meeting. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [it was enveloped in the cloud] or [the cloud rested on it]

The author assumes that readers will know this is **the cloud** that had been with the Israelites since their departure from Egypt and is described in Numbers 9:15–23. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the cloud that had previously been over the tent]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **glory**, you could express the same idea in another way. See how you translated this clause in verse 19. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh showed himself gloriously]

43.note: In a context such as this, your language might say “came” instead of **went**. Alternate translation: [And Moses and Aaron came]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the tent of meeting. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to the front of] or [to the area before]

45.note: Here, Yahweh is speaking as if Moses and Aaron could physically **lift** themselves up and take themselves away from the assembly. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Move far away]
The word **yourselves** is plural here because Yahweh is addressing Moses and Aaron, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is referring to death in a polite way by using the phrase **finish them**. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. See how you translated this clause in verse 21. Alternate translation: [and I shall end their lives] or [and I will make them experience death]

Here Yahweh is using **according to a moment** as a common expression of the culture to mean “instantly” or “immediately.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated this phrase in verse 21. Alternate translation: [instantly]

**Falling on their faces** was a symbolic action by which Moses and Aaron showed grief and submission to Yahweh. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. See how you translated this clause in verse 22. Alternate translation: [And they lay with their faces on the ground to show their grief] or [And they bowed with their faces to the ground in sorrow]

46.q: קַ֣ח אֶת־הַ֠⁠מַּחְתָּה וְ⁠תֶן־עָלֶ֨י⁠הָ אֵ֜שׁ מֵ⁠עַ֤ל הַ⁠מִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ וְ⁠שִׂ֣ים קְטֹ֔רֶת וְ⁠הוֹלֵ֧ךְ מְהֵרָ֛ה אֶל־הָ⁠עֵדָ֖ה וְ⁠כַפֵּ֣ר עֲלֵי⁠הֶ֑ם כִּֽי־יָצָ֥א הַ⁠קֶּ֛צֶף מִ⁠לִּ⁠פְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה הֵחֵ֥ל הַ⁠נָּֽגֶף
46.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these clauses, since the second set of clauses (**the wrath has gone out from to the face of Yahweh. The plague has begun**) gives the reason for the result that the first set of clauses describes (**Take the censer, and put fire on it from upon the altar, and set incense, and bring it quickly to the congregation, and make atonement for them**). Alternate translation: [The wrath has gone out from to the face of Yahweh. The plague has begun. Because of that, take the censer, and put fire on it from upon the altar, and set incense, and bring it quickly to the congregation, and make atonement for them]

The implication is that this is the same censer Aaron had used earlier when offering incense (see Numbers 16:6–7). You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [your censer] or [the censer you used earlier]

Here, **fire** represents burning coals from the altar. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. See how you translated the similar form in verse 7. Alternate translation: [embers]

By **from upon the altar**, Moses means from the altar of sacrifice where the sacred fire was kept burning. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [from upon the altar of sacrifice]
In a context such as this, your language might say “take” instead of **bring**. Alternate translation: [and take it]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **atonement**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and offer the incense to restore them to Yahweh]

Here, Moses is speaking of **the wrath** as if it were something that could physically move out from God. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh is angry and has sent punishment]

Here, **from to the face of Yahweh** represents coming from Yahweh’s presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from Yahweh’s presence]

Moses is not referring to a specific, known **plague**. He means a plague that is happening. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [A plague]

47.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And Aaron took a censer with fire in it]

The author is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [And indeed]

The author is not referring to a specific, known **plague**. He means a sickness or disease that had already begun. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [a plague]

The implication is that Aaron put the incense on the fire in the censer. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And he put the incense on the fire in the censer]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **atonement**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and he offered the incense to restore the people to Yahweh]

48.note: The implication is that Aaron positioned himself where he could stop the plague from spreading to the rest of the people. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And he stood where the plague was spreading, stationing himself between the people who were dying and the people who were still alive]

The expression **was restrained** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [And the plague stopped] or [And Yahweh restrained the plague]

49.note: Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [fourteen thousand seven hundred]

The implication is that Korah and his followers had rebelled against Moses and Aaron, and God had killed them because of their rebellion. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [because Korah and the people with him had rebelled]

50.note: Here the word **and** introduces what happened immediately before Aaron returned to Moses. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [once the plague had been restrained] or [as soon as the plague was restrained]
See how you translated this clause in 16:48. Alternate translation: [and the plague stopped] or [and Yahweh restrained the plague]
